Items.Authors: Kathryn M. Barrett, James Osborn, Noelia Martinez Rey, Domenico Bonaccini-Calia, Bernadett Stadler, David Jenkins
Items.Title: Simulation results for optical feeder link tilt pre-compensation using the LGS propagation delay method
Items.Abstract: We present successful numerical simulation results for uplink tilt pre-compensation for optical feeder links in ground-to-satellite optical communications. It is vital to pre-compensate the uplink beam at the point-ahead angle to ensure the stability of the link. A laser guide star (LGS) can measure the higher order modes at the point-ahead angle, giving an improvement in the data throughput, but with its inability to directly measure the tip and tilt modes, the optical link will still suffer frequent fades. We have developed the propagation delay method to be applied for optical communications. It is a technique to indirectly measure the tip and tilt from a sodium LGS, allowing for uplink tilt pre-compensation. Our numerical simulations show improvement in comparison to tilt pre-compensation using only the downlink tilt of the satellite. We intend to also explore how this method could be used to increase sky coverage for adaptive optics in astronomy.

Items.Authors: Ioannis Apergis, Daniel Bayliss, Paul Chote, James McCormac, Peter J. Wheatley, Edward M. Bryant, Jorge Fernández Fernández, Sam Gill, Leonidas Asimakoulas
Items.Title: Simultaneous observations of transiting exoplanets with a CCD and a scientific CMOS camera
Items.Abstract: Scientific CMOS cameras provide fast readout speeds and low read noise, offering clear advantages over traditional CCD detectors. In this work, we assess the performance of the Marana CMOS camera through simultaneous photometric observations of eight transiting exoplanets, taken alongside a CCD camera at the Next Generation Transit Survey (NGTS) facility at Paranal Observatory in Chile. The CMOS camera delivers white-noise dominated photometry, achieving ~500 ppm on 30-minute timescales, comparable to the CCD. Its significantly faster readout enables a ~20% increase in collected photons per duty cycle. These results demonstrate that modern CMOS detectors are well suited for high-precision, time-domain astronomical observations.

Items.Authors: Michela Todaro, Luisa Sciortino, Federico Fiorentino, Ugo Lo Cicero, Fabio D'Anca, Edoardo Alaimo, Tortorici Caterina, Pekka Törmä, Bahawal Haq, Matthew Soman, Pascal Mercère, Paulo Da Silva, Gabriele Minervini, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Daniele Brienza, Alfonso Collura, Salvatore Varisco, Claudio Saitta, Alberto Gulizzi, Gaspare Di Cicca, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Single- or multi-walled oriented or not carbon nanotube pellicles investigated for New Athena
Items.Abstract: CNT films are very promising as substrates for thermal and optical filters for X-ray or EUV detectors for space applications. This new technology is under evaluation as potential optical blocking and thermal filters for the ESA space mission New Athena. The main goal of this work is to compare the spectroscopic performance, in band (soft X-rays) and out-of-band (UV-VIS-MIR), of different kinds of CNT pellicles, namely randomly oriented dual layer single walled (SW), randomly oriented dual layer multi walled (MW), and oriented multiple layer MW. Based on this study, the appropriate CNT pellicle may be chosen to design a set of representative thin filter breadboards for the New Athena X-ray Integral Field Unit detector to achieve the Technology Readiness Level 5 before Athena Mission Adoption (February 2027).

Items.Authors: Robert Content, Yun Wang, Massimo Robberto, Gregory Wirth, Mark Dickinson, Thomas Greene, Jeffrey Kruck, Will Percival, Andreas Faisst, Lynne Hillenbrand, Jeyhan Kartaltepe, Nikhil Padmanabhan, Lado Samushia, Lee Armus, Florian Beutler, Andrew Benson, Micol Bolzonella, Samuel Brieden, Jarle Brinchmann, Emanuele Daddi, Kyle Finner, Andrew Hearin, Cullan Howlett, Jon Lawrence, Gregory Mosby, Eva-Maria Mueller, Seshadri Nadathur, Zoran Ninkov, Ken Osato, Casey Papovich, Jack Piotrowski, Lucia Pozzetti, Alvise Raccanelli, Jason Rhodes, Shun Saito, Hee-Jong Seo, Zachary Slepian, Stephen Smee
Items.Title: SIRMOS optical design and science: NIR spectroscopy of 100,000,000 galaxies at 1 < z < 4 and R~1300
Items.Abstract: SIRMOS (Satellite for Infrared Multi-Object Spectroscopy) is a NASA MIDEX mission concept to map the universe in 3D over ~500 cubic gigaparsecs using 100-million [OIII] and H-alpha emission line galaxies at 1< z<4. SIRMOS will probe the cosmic origin by placing constraints on primordial non-Gaussianity, precisely measure the sum of neutrino masses, and differentiate dark energy and modification of general relativity as the cause for the observed low-redshift cosmic acceleration. SIRMOS has a 60 cm aperture telescope with 0.9 square-degree field, and 2.2-million micromirrors on a digital micro-mirror devices (DMD) to provide a programmable reflective slit mask for spectroscopy at R~1300 over 1.25-2.5 microns. The multiplex advantage is 4000 even if the DMD is only 2048 micromirrors long. An alternate design uses a prism instead of a grating. Another uses a microshutter array instead of a DMD. The SIRMOS mission design is presented in a companion paper by Gregory Wirth.

Items.Authors: Johannes Wüthrich, Andrin Fazan, Sean MacBride, Marcelle Soares-Santos
Items.Title: Skipper CCD readout time optimization for astronomical applications
Items.Abstract: Skipper CCDs achieve noise reduction, relative to conventional CCDs, via repetitive measurements of pixel charge packets. However, this leads to an unavoidable increase in readout time, which often limits their application to astronomical instruments. To overcome this limitation, the optimal operation regime of Skipper CCDs must be determined, balancing noise improvement and readout time. We present a general optimization scheme derived from first principles and experimentally verified in the laboratory. Our results include analytical modeling of Skipper CCDs, based on their intrinsic noise power spectral density distribution. We further discuss the influence of clocking speed on the obtained results. Finally, we present measurements that validate our results, using a Skipper CCD from the Oscura experiment.

Items.Authors: Ebru UZUNÇAM, Onur Şatır, Cihan Tuğrul Tezcan, Elif Köksal, Muhammed Baki Bayram, Bilal ARSLAN, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Sky coverage statistics for DAG400 Telescope: natural guide star availability
Items.Abstract: This work focuses on the natural guide star (NGS) sky coverage for the 4-m DAG400 Telescope as it enters first light and primary operations. Since adaptive optics (AO) performance depends on finding an NGS of sufficient brightness within the required field of view, a statistical approach is used to determine practical limits. We analyze the probability of locating stars brighter than specific magnitude thresholds for the TROIA AO system—a flexible concept that adjusts corrected modes to atmospheric conditions and NGS brightness.

Items.Authors: Louis Gabarra, Fabrizio Cogato, Eduardo Medinaceli Villegas, Kerry Paterson, Mischa Schirmer
Items.Title: Snowballs detection in Euclid ’s NISP detectors
Items.Abstract: In this poster, we present an analysis of Euclid NISP dark images collected between August 2023 and June 2024 which aims to study the possible correlation of NISP artifacts referred to as snowballs with Solar energetic particles (SEP). Snowballs are bright transient events of mostly circular shape, with a nearly or fully saturated core, and covering tens to hundreds of pixels.  By exploiting an ad-hoc algorithm that combines the NISP signal and quality factor, snowballs and cosmic rays were identified in the NISP images. We present the detection rate of a population of about 40 000 snowballs, and an estimate of their energy.  We reveal an interesting correlation between SEP and snowballs, a still–mysterious bright, circular events with a nearly or fully saturated core, covering tens to hundreds of pixels.

Items.Authors: Laurel L. ONeill, Abraham D. Falcone, David M. Palmer, Md. Arman Hossen, Kadri M. Nizam, Lukas Stone, Ian Ashcroft, Brynn Bortree, Sierra Deppe, Timothy Emeigh, Killian Gremling, Gavin Houlihan, Katie McWhirter, Abigail Raytsis
Items.Title: source centroiding and angular resolution with BlackCAT and beyond
Items.Abstract: The Black hole Coded Aperture Telescope (BlackCAT) CubeSat. BlackCAT is a 6U CubeSat developed by the Pennsylvania State University optimized for the detection of high-redshift gamma-ray bursts (GRB), the detection of high-energy transient events, and detection and localization of electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave events. X-ray source centroiding of data from the Black hole Coded Aperture Telescope CubeSat and its angular resolution are discussed. The impacts and potential improvements from sub-pixel event repositioning will be discussed, as well as preliminary designs of a “mesh experiment” to investigate sub-pixel event localization and charge spreading.

Items.Authors: Pavel Shchekaturov, Linus Karl, Claudio Reinero, Christian Soenke, Robert Donaldson, Pablo Burgos, Cristian Herrera, Bogdan Jeram
Items.Title: SPARTA Upgrade RTC - Status Overview
Items.Abstract: “SPARTA Upgrade” is an obsolescence-mitigation project for the Standard Platform for Adaptive Optics Real-Time Control (SPARTA) Hard Real-Time Computer (HRTC), used on existing VLT instruments. Its goal is to replace the ageing platform with the latest high-performance COTS servers, combining new hardware technologies with modern real-time software programming techniques developed for the ELT, in order to achieve required performance.    The HRTC upgrade for existing systems such as AOF (GALACSI, GRAAL) and ERIS includes the replacement of the FPGA-based RTX box with a dual-socket Dell high-performance server based on modern multi-core AMD CPU architecture, the re-implementation of the SPARTA real-time core software, and an upgrade of the I/O hardware to modern PCIe cards while maintaining the sFPDP interfaces to the existing WFS cameras and DSM, and keeping the interfaces to the SPARTA co-processing cluster unchanged.

Items.Authors: Alexander Altmann, Pia Knopp, Norbert Meidinger, Robert Andritschke, Thomas Bechteler, Rafael Strecker, Jonas W. Mügge, Valeria Antonelli, Vadim Burwitz, Peter H. Lechner
Items.Title: Spectroscopic performance of the electrical functional models for the eXTP SFA-T detector
Items.Abstract: The Spectroscopy Focusing Array (SFA) is one of the three instruments on the eXTP satellite. It consists of six telescopes plus focal plane cameras, where five are equipped with a Silicon Drift Detector (SDD). These five SFA-T (T stands for timing) instruments are used for observations with high time resolution (≤ 10 µs), high throughput (dead time ≤ 5 % when observing a 1 Crab source), and good energy resolution (≤ 180 eV at 6 keV).  This paper presents the spectroscopic performance of the three Electrical Functional Models (EFM) for SFA-T that are assembled at the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE). A focus lies on the energy resolution at the planned sensor operating temperature of -45 °C after optimization of the SDD bias voltages.

Items.Authors: Hui Wang
Items.Title: Spot_Classification: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Fine-Grained Solar Active Region Magnetic Classification
Items.Abstract: We present Spot_Classification, a high-quality multimodal dataset for fine-grained magnetic classification of solar active regions. Built from SDO/HMI SHARP 720s data (2010–2024), it contains 17,253 co-aligned magnetogram–continuum image pairs across 2,507 active regions. Moving beyond the traditional Alpha/Beta/Beta-X scheme, it adopts a physically meaningful five-class system (including Beta-Delta, Beta-Gamma, and Beta-Gamma-Delta). Provided in both FITS and PNG formats, the data are split into training (12,512 pairs) and test (3,126 pairs) sets. Benchmark experiments with an improved U-Net achieve 89.42% and 88.15% accuracy on three- and five-class tasks, respectively. Rigorous quality control ensures a 98.1% valid record rate and minimizes projection distortion via ±75° solar disk centering. This dataset offers a robust foundation for sunspot recognition, multimodal learning, and large-model fine-tuning in solar physics and space weather forecasting.

Items.Authors: Peter Marley Chingaipe, Gyorgy Medgyesi, Alexandra Mazzoli, Emilie Bouzerand, Romain Laugier, Péter Ábrahám, Colin Dandumont, Denis Defrère, Adrian Glauser, Germain Garreau, Michael Ireland, András Joó, Jérôme Loicq, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Kwinten Missiaen, Manny Montoya, Johan Morren, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman, Warrick Schofield, Wannes Verstraeten
Items.Title: Status and performance of the Asgard/NOTT cold nulling camera
Items.Abstract: The Nulling Observations of dusT and PlaneTs (NOTT) instrument, part of the Asgard suite, will be the first nuller on the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI). Using long-baseline nulling interferometry in the L′-band (3.5–4.0 μm), NOTT suppresses stellar light to enable high-contrast imaging of exoplanets and circumstellar dust at high angular resolution. Its primary science goals include characterising hot/warm exozodiacal dust and detecting young Jupiter-like exoplanets at close (<10 AU) orbital separations. By combining light from up to four VLTI telescopes, NOTT will open new pathways for studying planetary formation environments and giant planet populations.

Items.Authors: Fabrizio Fornasiero
Items.Title: Straylight characterization and performance assessment for Phase A of the THESEUS mission
Items.Abstract: The THESEUS mission is a proposal for ESA’s M7 call and is currently undergoing Phase A assessment. The InfraRed Telescope (IRT), part of the mission payload, is an infrared instrument based on a Three-Mirror Anastigmat (TMA) design. In this work, we evaluate the impact of both in-field and out-of-field stray light. The primary sources of stray light are identified within the context of the mission, and their effects are quantified through empirical analysis and numerical simulations. The baffle geometry is optimized within the allocated envelope, and numerical simulations performed with FRED Optical are compared against theoretical models.

Items.Authors: Stefan J. Wijnholds, Tammo Jan Dijkema, Sarod Yatawatta
Items.Title: Streaming visibility processing for large radio interferometers
Items.Abstract: The temporal and spectral resolution of the raw visibility data of a radio interferometer is usually driven by the need to limit time and frequency smearing on the longest baseline and by measures to flag or remove interfering signals. Initial processing usually involves steps like flagging and (baseline-dependent) averaging, reducing the visibility data volume significantly. Streaming visibility processing (SVP) avoids intermediate storage of the (uncompressed) raw visibility data. This relaxes the requirements on the storage buffer size and access performance, thereby reducing its costs and permitting a more energy efficient solution. In this contribution, we present an SVP solution that we demonstrate with the ALMA correlator emulator and the LOFAR correlator. We also demonstrate that SVP enables near real-time processing by showing results from a low-latency imager for quality assurance in ALMA observations.

Items.Authors: Alex Drlica-Wagner, Alessio Taranto, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Joshua E. Meyers, Douglas R. Neill, John Andrew, Brian Stalder, Robert H. Lupton, Aashay Pai, Lee S. Kelvin, Aaron E. Watkins, Luca Rosignoli, Hannah M. Pollek, Anastasia Alexov
Items.Title: Study of a large-angle off-axis stray light path in Rubin Observatory commissioning
Items.Abstract: The most prominent and prevalent stray light features identified during the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory originate from large off-axis angles. Light from bright sources located >20 degrees off axis can pass between the mid-level and center-section light baffles on the Telescope Mount Assembly, reflect off of the primary mirror, and illuminate the LSST Camera focal plane. Due to delays in integration of the dome light–wind screen during construction, this scenario represents an unobstructed light path to the sky during Rubin Observatory commissioning. We describe the identification, modeling, characterization, and mitigation strategy for high-angle stray light artifacts at the Rubin Observatory.

Items.Authors: Takumi Togashi, Shuichi Gunji, Keito Watanabe, Haruaki Niinuma, Natsuki Kurooka, Daisuke Yonetoku, Tatsuya Sawano, Mutsumi Sugizaki, Makoto Arimoto, Hatsune Goto, Isshin Nagataka, Akihiro Doi, Hideo Matsuhara, Yoshimoto Maeda, Daiki Ishi, Hiroshi Tomida, Takanori Sakamoto, Motoko Serino, Tatehiro Mihara, Yusuke Kono, Hiroshi Akitaya, Hiroyuki Uchida
Items.Title: Study of detection algorithm for high-redshift GRBs to be observed by HiZ-GUNDAM/EAGLE
Items.Abstract: HiZ-GUNDAM is a future satellite mission aimed at exploring the early universe through observation of high-redshift gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). The satellite carries the wide-field X-ray monitor EAGLE, and the optical/near-infrared telescope MONSTER. When EAGLE detects an X-ray from transient sources, the onboard mission data processing unit (MPU) analyzes the event data and determines the source position.  To bring the target into MONSTER’s field of view, the MPU is expected to determine the GRB position within 1.5 arcmin based on the EAGLE data. We estimated the expected photon flux from high-redshift GRBs and X-ray backgrounds and simulated the resulting images using data from test experiments. Applying these results to the prototype GRB detection algorithm, we evaluated the expected localization performance.  In this conference, we report the current status of the X-ray image simulations and evaluate the performance of the detection algorithms based on these simulated datasets.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Runa A. Briguglio, Marco Xompero, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Armando Riccardi, Chiara Selmi
Items.Title: Subaperture calibration of deformable mirror for ELT-era DM size
Items.Abstract: In the VLT era, adaptive optics (AO) provided a major performance boost, but in the ELT era it has become essential. As primary mirrors grow, deformable mirrors (DMs) must also increase in size, requiring larger and more complex calibration facilities. Convex secondary DMs add further challenges, demanding larger optical beams for testing. This paper presents, to our knowledge, the first DM calibration performed in sub-aperture mode, where the mirror is never viewed in full clear aperture during calibration. This method enables the use of more compact and cost-effective test facilities, simplifying design, manufacturing, assembly, and calibration processes.

Items.Authors: Nicholas E. Thomas
Items.Title: SuperHERO (Super – High Energy Replicated Optics) X-ray telescope balloon mission
Items.Abstract: The SuperHERO hard X-ray telescope will observe extended sources at unprecedented imaging resolution, revealing the origins of non-thermal emission in extreme astrophysical environments. Employing NASA Marshall Space Flight Center’s replicated NiCo full-shell X-ray mirror technology to achieve better than 10-arcsecond half-power diameter (HPD) angular resolution on a balloon platform, SuperHERO consists of seven identical, co-aligned telescopes with a combined effective area of 45 cm² at 30 keV. SuperHERO was selected in the APRA 2023 call as a five-year mission, with an inaugural two-day flight scheduled from Fort Sumner, New Mexico, in the fall of 2028. For its initial target, SuperHERO will observe the Crab pulsar wind nebula, localizing hard X-ray emission. Mission development is currently underway, with updates and status to be provided in this presentation.

Items.Authors: Hangjian Liu, Bowen Yang, Xiangyi Gao, Danpei Zhao
Items.Title: Supervised Deep PSF Modeling for Wide-Field Telescope Imaging with Scarce Calibration Stars
Items.Abstract: The imaging quality of stars over a large field of view is fundamentally limited by the modeling accuracy of the point spread function (PSF). Most existing approaches are designed for small fields and degrade in challenging regimes such as sparse star fields, crowded regions, and coronagraphic occlusion, where suitable PSF calibration stars are scarce.  We propose a deep PSF-aware image enhancement framework. First, a supervised learning module learns a spatially varying wide-field PSF , thereby overcoming traditional small-field limitations. Second, a PSF posterior correction module is devised, which adaptively tunes the estimation strategy to alleviate model degradation.  Experiments conducted on the self-constructed simulation dataset demonstrate that this method significantly improves the PSF estimation accuracy, and outperforms the standard pipeline in both robustness and speed of star map matching.

Items.Authors: Shouwei Hu, Dehua Yang, Liang Chen, Cheng Liu
Items.Title: Support system design of the tertiary mirror of the 4-m JUST telescope
Items.Abstract: The Jiaotong University Spectroscopic Telescope (JUST) is a large optical telescope that requires a high-precision elliptical tertiary plano mirror. The support design of the mirror is crucial for its performance and stability. In this paper, we propose a novel support design method that combines lightweighting, 18 point whiffle-tree, and optimization techniques. We use finite element analysis to model the mirror and its support system, and optimize the parameters of the whiffletree to minimize the deformation and stress of the mirror. We conclude that our method is feasible and effective for the support design of the elliptical tertiary plano mirror of the JUST.

Items.Authors: Yanlyu Yang, Xin He, Xiaofei Li, Dehua Yang, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: System analysis of the 4-m Segmented JUST Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Jiaotong University Spectroscopic Telescope (JUST) a 4-m class telescope with the primary mirror segmented into 18 hexagonal sub-mirrors. This work develops an integrated system model that couples structural and optical performance analysis. A lean finite element model of the telescope, incorporating the simplified segmented mirror and support structure, was built to evaluate gravitational deflection, modal characteristics, and dynamic responses to wind and seismic loads. The resulting deformation fields were then reduced to piston and tip/tilt errors of the primary segments, secondary and the tertiary mirror and transferred to Zemax through a dedicated data-exchange interface. The telescope’s tracking and pointing accuracy was furtherly analyzed via induced aberrations. The fully coupled mechanical-optical model enabled direct propagation of perturbations into the optical system to evaluate final image quality and better understand telescope performance during design.

Items.Authors: Davide Vaccaro, Emanuele Taralli, Martin de Wit, Luciano Gottardi, Paul van der Hulst, Jan van der Kuur, Tobias Vos, Joseph S. Adams, Simon Bandler, Douglas Bennett, James Chervenak, Bertrand Doriese, Malcolm Durkin, Johnathon D. Gard, Carl Reintsema, Kazuhiro Sakai, Stephen Smith, Joel Ullom, Nicholas Wakeham, Roland H. den Hartog, Brian Jackson, Pourya Khosropanah, Aurora Simionescu
Items.Title: System performance of the sensor-readout chain in the development model of the focal plane assembly for Athena X-IFU
Items.Abstract: The X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) of ESA’s Athena observatory is designed to deliver high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with 2.5 eV energy resolution up to 7 keV and 5″ spatial resolution across the 0.2-12 keV band, using an array of 1500 TES with TDM readout. As part of our responsibility for the focal plane assembly (FPA), at SRON we have integrated and validated the sensor-readout chain for the X-IFU Demonstration Model (FPA-DM1.1), based on components delivered by VTT Finland, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) and by the National Institute of Standard and Technology (NIST).  In this contribution we present the first full sensor–readout chain performance characterization at system level of the FPA-DM1.1, which uses 4 TDM channels with 34 physical pixels each, operated in a TDM timing configuration representative of the flight baseline of 48-row multiplexing, which provides a co-added spectral performance at a level of 2.2 eV measured at 6 keV.

Items.Authors: Igor Petrucci, Carlos Lahoz, Diogo Batista
Items.Title: Systems thinking applied to the safety of the GMACS instrument for the Giant Magellan Telescope
Items.Abstract: GMACS, one of the first-generation instruments for the Giant Magellan Telescope, requires a systems-engineering perspective to ensure safe and reliable operation throughout its lifecycle. This work applies Systems Thinking and the Systems-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA) method to identify hazards associated with the slit-mask exchange mechanism, a critical subsystem for GMACS observations. The study examines the observatory’s organizational structure, its key stakeholders, and the safety plan defined by the GMTO, including its emphasis on human-factor hazards. The STPA application includes system modeling, identification of components, analysis of Unsafe Control Actions, and evaluation of potential hazards during both operation and preventive maintenance. The results show that integrating systems-theoretic methods strengthens hazard identification, supports safer operational procedures, and contributes to improving overall instrument reliability.

Items.Authors: Maggie Y. Kautz, Fernando E. Coronado, Austin Mears, Cameron C. Ard, Luke D. Mayer, Sanchit Sabhlok, Jane E. Morrison, Andre F. Wong, Douglas M. Kelly, Mike Eiklenborg, Heejoo Choi, Youngsik Kim, Patrick J. Ingraham, Nicholas J. Emerson, Mickael Rigault, Gudmundur K. Stefansson, Thomas Wevers, Daewook Kim, Catherine D. Merrill, Ewan S. Douglas
Items.Title: Technical status of the widefield context camera in the Lazuli Space Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Lazuli Space Observatory is a 3-meter aperture astronomical facility with a suite of instruments that will be utilized for rapid response observations. It is scheduled for launch in 2028. The Widefield Context Camera (WCC) is a 350–1000 nm multi-field imager spanning 35’ x 12’. This instrument provides both fine guidance and science capabilities. It is a mosaic of 23 commercial CMOS imagers with individual photometric filters. Two rows of Sony IMX 455 CMOS sensors will be used as science detectors, with two sensors defocused for wavefront sensing. One row of BAE HWK 4123 qCMOS sensors will be used for guiding and pointing. The HWK 4123 features a sub-electron readout noise (RON) that is pivotal for reaching >99% guide star availability in the field for rapid closing of the observatory fast-steering mirror (FSM) control loop. There are two instrument apertures within the mosaic, passing light to the ExtraSolar Coronagraph (ESC) and the Integral Field Spectrograph (IFS).

Items.Authors: Bortolino Saggin, Marco Giovanni Corti, Luca Oggioni, Marco Riva, Diego Scaccabarozzi, Luca Terenzi
Items.Title: Telescope design of the IRT instrument
Items.Abstract: The design of the IRT telescope has been carried-out during the phase A study of the Theseus mission. The reference IRT operation includes a slew maneuver from the S/C attitude adopted during the survey mode to the one needed to follow identified GRB sources, this in general creates a change in the environmental heat fluxes both on the telescope and the S/C determining a thermal transient. The main challenge in the IRT telescope design is therefore granting the optical performances throughout these thermal transients. The telescope design is based on a Korsch optical scheme identified during a previous study, with a 700 mm primary mirror diameter and a focal length of about 6 m. The preliminary tradeoff on materials have led to the combination of low CTE materials both for the optical elements and the structural ones i.e. Zerodur and mostly carbon fiber reinforced epoxy.

Items.Authors: Shi-hao Wang, Feng Zeng, Xingbo Wang, Yi-cheng Lin, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Temperature control system for scientific camera based on digital control and multi-stage TEC
Items.Abstract: In order to suppress the dark current of the detector and ensure the imaging quality of high-performance scientific cameras, a high-precision active temperature control system is constructed for the focal plane assembly. Methods of digital control and linear voltage driving for the thermoelectric cooler will be introduced. To accurately capture the thermal dynamics of the cooling system, high-resolution temperature acquisition is performed using a high-performance digital controller. And in order to achieve precise and continuous regulation of the driving voltage for the series load, a voltage-mode PID control method based on DAC-modulated DC-DC converter is carried out. The digital controller adjusts the reference voltage of the DC-DC via a DAC to linearly regulate the TEC voltage. Experimental verification shows that the system achieves temperature stability, which provides a data basis for the high-sensitivity imaging applications of future scientific cameras.

Items.Authors: Anabel C. Romero Hernandez, Chiaki Crews, Ben Dryer, Angaraj Duara, David J. Hall, Joan Requena, Jesper Skottfelt, Douglas Jordan
Items.Title: Testing CMOS image sensors for future space telescope missions
Items.Abstract: Future space telescope missions require high-resolution detectors that can measure light within a wide range of wavelengths. CMOS image sensors are being considered for such telescopes, with Teledyne e2v’s CIS300 family being a prime candidate. Missions such as ARRAKIHS and CASTOR, which aim to study dark matter and galaxy formation, have chosen the CIS300 as its main detector. Other missions considering the CIS300 include NASA’s Habitable Worlds Observatory, which aims to study earth-like planets. The CIS300 is a large area CMOS detector that detects light in the UV, visible and near-IR. The various settings and modes of operation of the CIS300 require testing, characterisation, and optimisation. A dedicated setup has been developed to conduct electro-optical tests that are underway, enabling the technology necessary for future space telescope missions.

Items.Authors: Claire G. Juramy-Gilles, Pierre Antilogus, Pierre Astier
Items.Title: The “dark dips” phenomenon in the LSST Camera on-sky images
Items.Abstract: When the LSST Camera started taking on-sky images at the Vera Rubin Observatory, some of the ITL STA3800 CCDs exhibited a previously undocumented effect. When a sufficiently bright star is superimposed over the sky background, the sensor columns that contain the star appear slightly darker than the background, both above and below the position of the star. This effect is not uniform across sensors, reaching an amplitude of up to seven percent of the background in the worst cases, but being undetectable in other sensors. For the affected sensors, the threshold required for the dips to become detectable also varies, from a few hundreds to a few thousands saturated pixels.

Items.Authors: Sebastiano Ligori, Vito Capobianco, Leonardo Corcione, Donata Bonino, Anna Di Giorgio, Scige Liu, Navin K. Shivapa Kamble
Items.Title: The application software for the Instrument Control Unit of the Ariel mission: design and testing approach
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present the current status of the development of the application software of the Instrument Control Unit of the Ariel mission, which has the objective to obtain spectra for a number of transiting exoplanets. The Instrument Control Unit provides Command and Control functionalities for the AIRS spectrograph and the Telescope Control Unit, which is used to control and move the secondary mirror mechanism and provides the telescope temperatures.  We will illustrate the main functionalities of the software as well as the approach we are using for testing at different level, from static analysis to unit tests, to functional tests.

Items.Authors: Jyotirmay Paul, Daniel Lancaster, Sorabh Chhabra, Stefan Kraus, Michael Ireland, Owain Snaith, John Monnier, Daniel Ahrer
Items.Title: The Asgard/BIFROST pre-injection optics and fibre injection module: revision of optomechanical design & lab and on sky results
Items.Abstract: The Asgard/BIFROST instrument at the VLTI will enable high-spectral-resolution interferometry across 1.0 µm (Y, J, H bands). Its pre-injection optics correct for birefringence and longitudinal dispersion, while the fibre-injection module compresses beams into single-mode fibres. A fibre-switching module allows injection into photonic devices optimized for different wavebands. We present a comprehensive revision of the optical and optomechanical design, including redesigned mounting interfaces, refined pupil positioning, and enhanced mechanical stability to improve alignment strategy and fibre-coupling efficiency. Laboratory characterization shows significant gains in efficiency, stability, and repeatability, with on-sky commissioning results to be presented. The upgraded system provides a stable, high-throughput system to the Asgard/BIFROST.

Items.Authors: Saverio Lombardi, Fabrizio Lucarelli
Items.Title: The ASTRI Mini-Array Project data processing system: main components, functionalities and interfaces
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI Mini-Array Project, led by INAF, is building nine 4-m class Cherenkov telescopes at the Teide Observatory, Spain. Seven telescopes are already installed, with two of them currently undergoing the commissioning and science verification phase.  The ASTRI project features the data processing system (DPS), a dedicated system for the end-to-end data processing and scientific exploitation. Raw data are immediately transferred from on site to the ASTRI data center in Rome (Italy) via high-speed network. The DPS employs a multi-stage pipeline on a HPC cluster to perform data pre-processing, calibration, reduction, and analysis, aiming for fast, reliable, and reproducible generation of science-ready products (event-lists and IRFs) and preliminary science products.  This contribution overviews the main DPS components, functionalities, and interfaces, and presents results from its current development and testing using commissioning data of the first group of telescopes in the array.

Items.Authors: Bachar Wehbe, Alexandre Cabral, Nicolas Blind
Items.Title: The atmospheric dispersion corrector of RISTRETTO: a closed-loop concept
Items.Abstract: With the complexity of new instruments like RISTRETTO, it is essential to simplify how an ADC works and how we will guarantee satisfaction with the requirements. A new simple method is proposed for the case of RISTRETTO. In this paper, we will present the concept behind this closed-loop concept, as well as the preliminary design of the ADC.

Items.Authors: Claudio Macculi, Luigi Piro, Matteo D'Andrea, Giacomo Gorla, Simone Lotti, Gabriele Minervini, Flavio Gatti, Marcello Celasco, Lorenzo Ferrari Barusso, Daniele Grosso, Manuela Rigano, Mauro Fiorini, Michela C. A. Uslenghi, Guido Torrioli, Fabio Chiarello, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Chiara Grappasonni, Simonetta Puccetti, Angela Volpe, Paolo Bastia, Francesco Villa, Artur Cardoso Coimbra
Items.Title: The Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector for the Athena X-IFU instrument: status towards the TRL5
Items.Abstract: The Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector (CryoAC) is a particle detector aimed at increasing the X-IFU instrument sensitivity, a cryogenic TES microcalorimeter on-board the Athena mission, the next ESA X-ray Large mission planned for the Adoption in early 2027. Athena will host two complementary instruments optimized for energy resolution and FoV: the X-IFU and the WFI. The X-IFU main TES array detector, a high-grade imaging spectrometer, cannot distinguish among in-band energy depositions from charged particles crossing its absorbers, the Non X-ray Background (NXB), and the X-ray photons that make the scientific signal. The CryoAC will detect these charged particles thus enabling NXB level of 5E-3 cts/cm2/s/keV. It is a 4-pixel TES based microcalorimeter detector operating at 50 mK developed by an Italian team made by ASI, INAF, Genova University and CNR/IFN Roma. In this contribution we present the current status of CryoAC development toward TRL5, and outline the programmatic roadmap.

Items.Authors: Mariachiara Celato, Paul Hedderman, Christoph Tenzer, Andrea E. Santangelo, Hannah Lerman, Melissa McHugh, Ian Hutchinson, Paul T. O'Brien
Items.Title: The data processing pipeline for the THESEUS soft X-ray imager
Items.Abstract: The THESEUS mission is designed to detect Gamma-Ray Bursts, X-ray transients, and infrared afterglows in order to probe the high-redshift Universe and advance time-domain and multi-messenger astrophysics. Its scientific capabilities rely on a coordinated payload, including the Soft X-ray Imager (SXI). This contribution presents the SXI data-processing pipeline developed during the ESA M7 Phase A study. The SXI consists of two wide-field lobster-eye cameras covering the 0.3 to 5 keV energy band and producing high-speed data streams that require efficient onboard processing. We outline the detection and imaging chain, describe the modelling of the lobster-eye PSF and the localisation method, and detail the logic and expected performance of the onboard transient trigger algorithm.

Items.Authors: David A. Girou, Alex Bayerle, Adam Lassise, Aniket Thete, Aidan Wilson, Boris Landgraf, Bruno N. Menezes, Christian Körnig, Chris Rizos, Casper van Aarle, Donny de Borst, Danilo Ocana Garcia, Enrico Hauser, Faduma Yuusufali, Giuseppe Vacanti, Jasper den Hollander, Jelle Guijt, Khalid Lahmidi, Katharina Witte, Luigi Castiglione, Loes Crama, Laurens Keek, Luc Voruz, Marloes Bistervels, Maximilien J. Collon, Mark Vervest, Nicolas M. Barrière, Noë Eenkhoorn, Noë Eenkhoorn, Paulo da Silva Ribeiro, Patrick de Vries, Ramses Günther, Sofia Fuster Almenar, Sebastian Obwaller, Vivien Hoinkis, Yvette Jenkins, Marcos Bavdaz, Habib Boualam, Pieter Smid, Bart Schurink, Arenda Koelewijn, Jeroen Haneveld, Mark Olde Riekerink, Mathijs Bosman, Maurice Wijnperlé, Michael Krumrey, Dieter Skroblin, Levent Cibik, Robert Fechner, Vadim Burwitz, Sara Svendsen, Desirée Della Monica Ferreira, Diego Paredes-Sanz, Finn E. Christensen, Nolann Ravinet, Sonny Massahi, George Floros, Andrew Rees, Chris Adam, Ethan Dunnell, Kevin Ball, Dominique Heinis, Alejandro Sanchez , Antonio Carballedo, Joan Torras, Marc Sanchez, Norman Niewrzella, Holger Lasser, Bianca Salmaso, Alberto Moretti, Daniele Spiga, Davide Sisana, Stefano Basso
Items.Title: The development of the NewAthena X-ray mirror modules
Items.Abstract: NewAthena is the next generation X-ray observatory being prepared by the European Space Agency (ESA) as an L-class mission for adoption in 2027. It will operate from 0.2 to 10 keV and use a 2.6 m diameter optic populated by several hundred Silicon Pore Optics (SPO) mirror modules. The SPO mirror modules are developed by ESA, cosine, and partners, and target an angular resolution better than 9 arc-seconds with an effective area above 1 m² at 1 keV. The program is now ramping up production while finalizing the remaining process parameters needed for a stable industrial flow. Current work focuses on three rows (row-08, row-15, row-01) and on balancing competing drivers such as effective area, angular resolution, cost, and schedule. This paper presents the status of SPO mirror module production and the preparation for full-scale manufacturing ahead of mission adoption.

Items.Authors: Laurent Ravera, Jan Soucek, Frédéric Pinsard, Yann Parot
Items.Title: The Digital Readout Electronics (DRE) of the X-IFU instrument aboard NewAthena
Items.Abstract: The Digital Readout Electronics (DRE) plays a critical role in signal acquisition and processing from the Transition Edge Sensor (TES) array. Developed for Time Domain Multiplexing (TDM) readout, this system builds on experience from Frequency Domain Multiplexing prototypes and addresses the challenges specific to high-resolution X-ray detection. The DRE is responsible for generating row selection signals, sampling pixel error outputs, and producing feedback and dynamic offset compensation signals to ensure accurate readout from the MUX SQUIDs. It performs real-time event detection, extracting 8192-sample data records at a sampling frequency of 130.2 kHz, and processes them to determine photon arrival time, energy, and event grade. Final photon energy values are calibrated on-ground using gain scale corrections.

Items.Authors: Brian T. Fleming, Kevin France, Allison Youngblood
Items.Title: The ESCAPE extreme and far-ultraviolet spectrograph for measuring the irradiance and coronal mass ejections from exoplanet host stars
Items.Abstract: The Extreme-ultraviolet Stellar Characterization for Atmospheric Physics and Evolution (ESCAPE) small explorer mission concept is designed to measure the extreme- and far-ultraviolet (EUV and FUV; 80 - 1650 angstrom) irradiance and flare activity of exoplanet host stars; essential measurements for assessing the stability of rocky planet atmospheres in the habitable zone. The ESCAPE design consists of a fixed optical configuration with a grazing incidence “Hettrick- Bowyer” telescope feeding grazing and normal incidence spectroscopic channels. We report on the ESCAPE design, projected performance and mission implementation plan for the first major NASA EUV astrophysics mission in nearly 30 years.

Items.Authors: Jordan M. Stone, Craig Kulesa, Steve Ertel, Suresh Sivanandam, Tim Hardy, Phil Hinz, Jarron Leisenring, Josh Eisner, Charles E. Woodward, Manny Montoya, Brian Hicks
Items.Title: The Fast Fringe Tracking Camera (FFTCam): an upgraded infrared fringe tracker for the Large Binocular Telescope Interferometer
Items.Abstract: We report the first on-sky results using an upgraded infrared fringe-tracker for the Large Binocular Telescope Interferometer (LBTI), which combines light from two 8.4 meter mirrors on a common mount. Previously, co-phased interferometric observations with the LBT were restricted to stars with K<5, due to sensitivity limitations with the fringe tracking camera. In the last year we successfully replaced the old fringe-tracking detector with a newer device, a 320x256 pixel Leonardo Saphira array, which will provide greatly enhanced sensitivity, improving the fringe-tracking limit by several magnitudes. Our presentation details our implementation approach and early performance characterization. We also discuss the scientific prospects of more sensitive co-phased LBTI observations that yield the equivalent resolution of a 23-m aperture over a 20''x20'' field of view at wavelengths spanning J-band to N-band.

Items.Authors: Juliana X. Barstow, Nicholas Kruczek, Kevin France, Nicholas Nell, Patrick Behr, Emily Farr, Stefan Ulrich
Items.Title: The FLUID sounding rocket: instrument development and assembly update
Items.Abstract: The Far- and Lyman-Ultraviolet Imaging Demonstrator (FLUID) is a rocket-borne multi-band UV imaging instrument spanning 92-193 nm with arcsecond-level resolution. It’s four imaging channels use custom reflective multi-layer coatings aligned with initial Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) specifications. FLUID will observe nearby galaxies to study how massive stars shape chemical and dynamical feedback, providing the first morphological classification of nearby galaxies in the Lyman UV.   The four-channel design is optimized to break age-dust degeneracy while limiting geocoronal or interplanetary Lyα emission. Each channel is a Cassegrain telescope with reflective narrow band coatings, achieving < 4.2″ resolution (~100 pc). Two channels, F110M and F140M, are assembled and aligned, meeting requirements with >90% margin.   We summarize science goals, instrument design, and calibration results, including new alignments for the F160M and F180M. FLUID remains on track for launch in early 2027.

Items.Authors: Yixian Cao
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: the Imaging Data Reduction Pipeline
Items.Abstract: The MICADO instrument will provide the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) with first-light diffraction-limited near-infrared imaging capabilities. As a key component of the instrument's data flow system, the MICADO data reduction software is designed to process raw scientific and calibration data for instrument health monitoring and scientific analysis. Within the data reduction software, the imaging pipeline is specifically developed to support data processing of MICADO's imaging observations. The pipeline is being developed within the European South Observatory (ESO) software framework. Central to the imaging pipeline are eight reduction recipes, each implemented using the CPL plugin interface to ensure seamless integration with ESO's front-end systems. These recipes are designed to transform raw input data into master calibration and science products through a systematic processing approach. Ultimately, the pipeline removes detector effects and generates photometrically and astrometric

Items.Authors: Sebastiano Spinello, Alessandro Costa, Federico Incardona, Kevin Munari, Emilio Mastriani, Fulvio Gianotti, Ismam Abu, Marcello Lodi, Alessandro Tacchini, Marco De Benedetto, Andrea Mandica
Items.Title: The new version of the ASTRI Mini-Array Alarm System
Items.Abstract: Within the ASTRI Mini-Array SCADA infrastructure, the Alarm System detects, prioritises, and notifies abnormal conditions that may affect the safety and performance of telescopes, auxiliary devices, and ICT infrastructure. In October 2025 it completed its transition from an ACS-embedded component to a stand-alone Java application, improving modularity, deployment, and independence from the ALMA Common Software (ACS) middleware. The new architecture is centred on an Alarm Manager that aggregates alarms from OPC-UA (Open Platform Communications – Unified Architecture) servers, ACS Notification Channels, and ICT subsystems, with configuration data managed in the System Configuration Database (SCDB). RESTful APIs expose configuration, status, and alarm information to the Human Machine Interface (HMI) and higher-level orchestration software.

Items.Authors: Peter W. G. Byrnes, Glen Herriot, Emma Rautio-Roe, Jean-Pierre Veran
Items.Title: The NFIRAOS vibration budget
Items.Abstract: Equipment vibrations are known to degrade performance at many astronomical observatories. The Thirty Meter Telescope project has developed a vibration budget, which specifies maximum allowable forces for potential sources of vibration. The first light Narrow-Field Infra-Red Adaptive Optics System (NFIRAOS) has been allocated a total vibration force of 1.12 Newtons (rms) by this budget.    The NFIRAOS project team has apportioned this allocation to various subsystems comprising NFIRAOS. This paper will summarize the NFIRAOS vibration budget and the current basis for these terms, including a description of simulations and laboratory tests of prototype equipment, that have been conducted or are planned.

Items.Authors: Benoît Neichel, Vincent Chambouleyron, Lorenzo Busoni, Romain Fetick, Angelie Alagao, Francois Leroux, Mathieu Motte, Charlotte Bond, Cedric Heritier, Lisa-Marie Mazzolo, Jean-Francois Sauvage, Prashant Pathak, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Pierre Jouve, Jean-Pierre Veran, Carlos Correia, Markus Kasper, Peter Wizinowich, Michele Cirasuolo, Jason Spyromilio, Pierre Vernazza, Armando Riccardi, Simone Esposito, Thierry Fusco, Giovanni Cresci, Guiliana Fiorentino, Morgan Gray, Jean-Luc Gach, Marc Ferrari, Anne-Marie Galliano, Jacopo Farinato, Davide Greggio, Fernando Pedichini
Items.Title: The observing with adaptive optics school: training the next generation of AO scientists and engineers
Items.Abstract: We have established a new international Adaptive Optics (AO) School offering early-career researchers a hands-on introduction to modern AO. Held annually at OHP, the program combines expert lectures with laboratory work and night observations on PAPYRUS, a fully functional AO bench.    Students learn key AO concepts—turbulence, wavefront sensing, control, real-time computing, DMs, and laser guide stars—while gaining practical experience operating the PAPYRUS system. Nearly 80 participants from four continents have already attended, valuing the strong interaction with AO specialists from major institutes.    In 2026, the school will move to the Asiago Observatory with the permanent installation of PAPYRUS, expanding observing opportunities and strengthening ties with the Italian AO community. This relocation supports the long-term goal of establishing a European training platform for future AO experts.

Items.Authors: Rosario Cosentino, Mauro Focardi, Anna Maria Di Giorgio, Andrea Russi, Giovanni Giusi, Simone Chiarucci, Carlo Del Vecchio Blanco, Luca Serafini, Gunter Laky, Dominik Loidolt, Harald Ottacher, Harald Jeszenszky, Roland Ottensamer, Devitt Dini, Giuseppe Giglio, Armin Luntzer, Alessio Pannocchia, Marco Passerai, Marina Vela Nuñez, Marco Verna, Luca Pilato, Natalia Auricchio, Maria Farina, Scigè John Liu
Items.Title: The PLATO Instrument Control Unit: from qualification to flight integration and final readiness
Items.Abstract: The PLATO Instrument Control Unit (ICU), the payload’s on-board computer for data handling and lossless compression, has completed its qualification and reached flight status. Developed by INAF and Kayser Italia with contributions from IWF Graz and the University of Vienna, the ICU has evolved from Engineering Models to the Proto-Flight Model (PFM), now integrated into the payload. We present the final ICU configuration and the key results of the PFM functional, environmental, and EMC test campaigns. Particular emphasis is placed on the performance of the hardware–software compression chain, verification of redundancy and SpaceWire interfaces, and validation of the flight Application Software. The results confirm compliance with PLATO requirements and demonstrate full readiness of the ICU for launch.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Novelli
Items.Title: The Simons Observatory: signal characterization of the POLOCALC drone-based artificial calibration source: modelling, performances, and prospects
Items.Abstract: We present an analysis of time-ordered data collected while flying the POLOCALC source in the far field of Simons Observatory's Small Aperture Telescopes. We discuss an analytical model of the drone-plus-source emission collected by the detectors and then we compare it with experimental data. We analyze a double-demodulation approach to perform an absolute polarisation angle calibration of the detectors. This pipeline allows to isolate the calibration source emission from the data and determine the polarisation angle measured by the detectors as a function of time. After discussing the methodology from a theoretical standpoint, we validate it numerically and we perform Monte-Carlo simulations to determine the achievable $\theta_{pol}$ sensitivity within one drone crossing. We then discuss and assess possible sources of systematic bias in this type of measurement. Finally, time-domain-based measurements of the source's $\theta_{pol}$ are presented.

Items.Authors: Nadia Dachlythra
Items.Title: The Simons Observatory: the first reported beam chromaticity measurements for a CMB experiment (courtesy of POLOCALC)
Items.Abstract: The Simons Observatory (SO) Small Aperture Telescopes observe the CMB in six wide, ~25% bandwidth frequency channels, but key instrument properties—especially the beam—vary significantly across each band. Traditional beam calibration, based on planet observations, provides only band-averaged beams and is limited by the scarcity of suitable astrophysical sources. This restricts the instrument modeling accuracy needed for precise B-mode measurements. To address this, we use POLOCALC, a drone-borne, narrow-band, polarized thermal source deployed in the Atacama desert. We report results from two 2025 campaigns, presenting what we believe are the first measurements of beam chromaticity in a CMB instrument, focusing on the critical 90GHz frequency band. These measurements introduce an unprecedented level of sensitivity to instrument modelling.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Paonni, Alessandro Di Filippo, Ivan Agostinelli, Dietrich Pescoller, Mauro Centrone, Marco Faccini, Roberto Biasi, Laura Salvi
Items.Title: The Station Control Software for the ASI Space Debris Laser Ranging Project
Items.Abstract: The Station Control Software (SCS) is the supervisory core of the Italian Space Agency’s Space Debris Laser Ranging (SDLR) station, coordinating all subsystems involved in high-precision debris detection and ranging. It unifies control of telescope tracking, laser guide star generation, adaptive optics loops, laser-ranging sequences, diagnostics, and safety functions. The SCS combines hard real-time tasks—such as wavefront correction and timing synchronization—with soft real-time sequencing, monitoring, and data management. Its modular architecture supports multiple operational modes and autonomous handling of scheduling, system health, and laser safety. A dedicated GUI enables intuitive operation, ensuring reliable and continuous performance of the SDLR facility.

Items.Authors: Drew M. Miles, Chris Martin, Laura Jones-Wilson, Mateusz Matuszewski, Vincent Picouet, Paul Eryan, Gillian Kyne, Adam Johnson, Ian McKinley, Shouleh Nikzad, Joseph D. Perez, Cameron Wheeler
Items.Title: The Stratospheric Cosmic Web Imager technical implementation
Items.Abstract: The Stratospheric Cosmic Web Imager (SCWI) is a new stratospheric balloon instrument designed to detect and characterize emission from the circumgalactic medium (CGM) and interagalactic medium (IGM). Designed as a superpressure balloon mission, SCWI plans for tens of nights of UV spectroscopic observations from an altitude of ≈32km, allowing sensitivity from ≈195-215nm. Within this band, SCWI aims to detect and spectroscopically characterize emission from the CGM/CQM of several galaxies at redshifts z < 1, and spend several nights on deep-field IGM observations to detect, for the first time, IGM emission in the UV band. We present here the SCWI mission concept, science objectives, and instrument overview.

Items.Authors: Alessio Turchi, Elena Pancino, Aleksandra Avdeeva
Items.Title: The survey of surveys: new machine learning parameters data release
Items.Abstract: Building upon our previous Survey of Surveys (SoS) effort to derive spectroscopic-quality stellar parameters from photometry using machine learning (ML), we present a significant expansion of our SoS-ML catalog. In our first release, we demonstrated that a ML method trained on the calibrated SoS-Spectro catalog could predict accurate stellar parameters (Teff, log g, and [Fe/H]) from Gaia, SDSS and SkyMapper photometry, achieving notable improvements over existing ML catalogs, particularly for metal-poor stars. This multi-survey approach leverages complementary wavelength coverage to improve parameter determination. In this work, we substantially broaden our photometric coverage by incorporating other catalogs such as 2MASS and Pan-STARRS, and an improved SoS-Spectro. This will extend our catalog, especially in poorly covered regions. We also aim to provide more robust parameter estimates, especially for challenging stellar populations, such as cool giants and metal-poor halo stars.

Items.Authors: Enrico Bozzo
Items.Title: The THESEUS IRT filter wheel mechanism
Items.Abstract: In this contribution we will provide an overview of the THESEUS IRT filter wheel mechanism. We will describe the current status of the mechanism design, as well as the technological challenges and recent advancements.
